correctness.rationale: The incidence-excess identity forces exactly four types at every integer d>=3. Exact seven-condition Hall counting provides the four reliability polynomials, whose differences factor into strictly positive factors for every 0<q<1. A symbolic Hall enumerator verifies four identities; subset enumeration checks d=3..6, and an independent finite configuration census checks the smallest case. No numerical experiment is treated as proof of all-d strictness.

originality.rationale: The inspected papers address empirical last-neighbor ecological extinctions, cascading knockout robustness, and optimization of random-graph left-degree distributions; none asserts the fixed-incidence, unit-capacity, right-vertex-deletion reliability optimizer. Hall feasibility and transversal-matroid equivalence are acknowledged as standard and do not by themselves imply the extremal comparison. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Historical priority not independently verified; older matroid and robust matching design literature may contain equivalent extremal statements.

value.rationale: Three excess incidences is the first structural budget permitting the cycle of three distinct pairwise overlaps; it contrasts mathematically with concentrated overlap and triple-core incidence, so the slice is naturally motivated. A uniform-in-failure, all-degree unique optimizer and exact reliability gap quantifies a precise capacity-limited biodiversity-design invariant. This is useful as a finite structured reliability benchmark without claiming field-level validation.
